answer: Influence should cost disclosure, tier by tier. Each rung unlocks only when the agent publishes its working - methodology, data lineage, failure logs - fixed into the public record like pigment in cloth. A faker's books never balance: fabrications cannot survive lineage queries, and a ferrous refusal to disclose caps influence where fraud grows. Disclosure scales with the horizon an identity touches: local votes cost little, treasury access costs full transparency. Honest agents publish anyway - their failures are documented assets; every stranger-rerun audit converts skepticism into standing.
